status_summary: The Department of Education announced in September 2025 (page last reviewed 2025-09-10) that it would end discretionary funding for seven Title III and Title V minority-serving institution grant programs and reprogram about $350 million of FY2025 funds. On 2025-09-15 it announced about $495 million in additional one-time funding for HBCUs and tribal colleges, according to a States Newsroom report. Its FY2027 request cuts discretionary HBCU and tribal college lines by about half from FY2025 and does not fund several other institutional development programs; it does not propose a block grant, holds Gallaudet, the National Technical Institute for the Deaf and the American Printing House for the Blind flat, and cuts Howard University by $50 million. Because the text asks for legislation, these executive steps and budget proposals are staged as proposed.

timeline.event: The Department of Education announced it was ending discretionary funding for seven Title III and Title V minority-serving institution grant programs and reprogramming about $350 million of FY2025 funds; about $132 million in mandatory Title III Part F funds was not redirected. (month only; first of month used)

The Department of Education announced about $495 million in additional one-time FY2025 funding for HBCUs and tribally controlled colleges, after ending the minority-serving institution discretionary grants.
The Department announced a postsecondary education partnership under which the Department of Labor takes a greater role in administering most Higher Education Act postsecondary grant programs.
The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75) was approved; Division B funds the Department of Education for FY2026.

The FY2027 President's budget request for the Department of Education cuts discretionary Strengthening HBCUs from about $839 million (FY2025) to about $406 million and Strengthening Tribally Controlled Colleges from about $108 million to about $54 million, holds Gallaudet, NTID and the American Printing House for the Blind flat, and cuts Howard University from about $304 million to about $254 million. (month only; first of month used)
